fields.narrative_intro: *A haunted person and an overconfident person discuss AI agents painting arrows on screens inside a Zoom waiting room for all eternity.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
HAUNTED PERSON: "Claude Code refactored a monorepo, then printed “please click Allow” unseen."
fields.panel2:
[build]
OVERCONFIDENT PERSON: "Use big-arrow: glowing arrows, boxes, and text, directly onscreen."
HAUNTED PERSON: "539 GitHub stars; roughly 400 arrived in two days."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
OVERCONFIDENT PERSON: "It evaluated 26 tools and uses just 1.4% CPU."
HAUNTED PERSON: "Now it needs permission to point at its permission."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: Giant arrow points to ALLOW; tiny arrow points to giant arrow; Zoom says FOREVER.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
HAUNTED PERSON: "The least intelligent part of the AI stack is now middle management."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: A permission box asks, “Allow big-arrow to display this arrow?” Its tiny arrow points to YES.]

narrative_summary: Big-arrow solves an AI agent’s human-click problem by creating a permission loop in the eternal Zoom waiting room.
rationale: Candidate 1 turns the tool's actual permission problem into a sharper, less obvious middle-management analogy, then escalates it with a recursive permission button. The other two are visually clear and fact-specific, but their closing beats mostly restate the setup or lean on weaker star/“proud of it” wordplay.
story_title: Show HN: Let your AI agents paint big arrows, boxes and text on your screen
place: inside a Zoom waiting room for all eternity
hat_pair: crash helmet with a tiny windshield wiper on the visor
foam binoculars worn as an oversized hat with two giant lens holes staring outward
